messages:
maria: Follow-up from yesterday's RFC review: we need an operations playbook for overlay rollouts that include precision changes (FP8/INT8/4-bit). I sketched a minimal set of steps, please critique.

nik: TL;DR please? can we keep it <6 steps :grin:?

maria: Sure — high level: 1) dry-run eval (shadow) 2) staged canary with soft-warmup 3) traffic-weighted warmup sampling 4) quality monitors + circuit breaker 5) rollback + postmortem.

leo: Important: call out billing and deduping. Soft-warmup can double token compute briefly; we must surface estimated cost to customer and to internal chargeback.

tara: Also need explicit guard against KV-layout changes. If overlay changes KV key shape we should reject at validation time.

maria: Agreed. Draft validation rules: no tensor shape change, no attention-head count change, only qscheme/scales/clip tweaks allowed. Validation service should return one-line reason on reject.

nik: For warmup sampling percentages: propose deterministic algorithm: sample X% of unique user sessions (not tokens) to hit distribution of prefixes. Start X=2% for low-risk overlays, X=10% for aggressive low-bit transitions.

leo: We should also use frequency-aware warmup: pick the top N prefixes by 24h frequency and always warm those. That covers majority of cold-start tail.

maria: Good. What about canary duration? I think 30 minutes minimum for latency stability, but quality metrics may need more — 4 hours for meaningful regression signals on some endpoints.

tara: Put that in the playbook as configurable per-route. Add an auto-extend if quality signals are noisy.

nik: Circuit-breaker thresholds: two levels: hard (latency > p99 baseline + 200ms or error spike) and soft (quality delta > 1.5% measured by BLEU/ROUGE-like metric or our degscore). Soft trigger should notify and auto-throttle traffic to 10% until investigated.

leo: How do we compute quality delta in near-real-time? We can use shadow sampling against prompt bank for quick signal and compare model outputs with golden responses. Need to publish latency of that pipeline (expect ~15min lag).

maria: Ops UI requirement: show active overlay id, applied routes, warmup progress, estimated additional cost (tokens * price uplift), and an easy "pause/warmup-only" toggle.

nik: Security/RBAC: overlays should be changable by: SRE, customer-admin (for enterprise), and product for experiments. All updates logged with diff and checksum.

tara: Implementation note: runtime must expose API: `POST /overlays/apply?dry_run=true` returning {accepted:bool, reasons:[], predicted_cost_delta: "12.4%"}. Keep response tiny.

maria: Nice. Example mini-overlay format we agreed on in RFC: `{"v":1, "overrides": {"weight_qscheme":"int8","act_clip":3.2}}` Keep it under 2KB.

leo: One more: backward compatibility with older runtimes. If runtime doesn't understand overlay keys, treat as reject unless overlay has `compat_mode: "ignore-unknown-keys"` and customer explicitly opts-in. Document risk.

nik: Action items:
- m: update playbook with sampling defaults + canary durations
- l: prototype cost estimator for soft-warmup delta
- t: add validation endpoint + RBAC sketch
- n: wire alerting templates for soft/hard trips

maria: Timeline: aim for staging prototype next sprint. I'll open the playbook doc and tag the owners.

ops-bot: Deploy log: overlay-playbook-v1 pushed to docs (id d-782). Canary rollout scheduled for staging at 2026-04-02T09:00Z.

maria: Thanks all. If no objections I'll attach the playbook link once it's live and mark this RFC follow-up as closed.
